title: HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (India)
specialty: Infectious Diseases / Occupational Health / Emergency Medicine

evidenceAudit.scope: Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) after occupational (needlestick, splash) and non-occupational (sexual, including sexual assault) exposure in India: first aid, risk assessment, timing, the three-drug regimen, baseline and follow-up tests, hepatitis B and C, and transition to pre-exposure prophylaxis. The NACO National Guidelines for HIV Care and Treatment (2021) section 2.10 could not be opened, so WHO (2024), CDC (2025) and the WHO-prequalified TLD label are used.
findings: Start as soon as possible, ideally within 24 hours and no later than 72 hours; 28-day course; three drugs preferred (WHO 2024 summary).

Dolutegravir plus tenofovir plus lamivudine or emtricitabine as a preferred regimen; baseline HIV, hepatitis B, creatinine, ALT, AST and pregnancy tests; HIV testing at 4–6 and 12 weeks (CDC 2025, Appendix A).

TLD (dolutegravir/lamivudine/tenofovir DF 50/300/300 mg) one tablet daily for 28 days for PEP, 30 kg or more; not with creatinine clearance below 50 mL/min; dolutegravir 50 mg twice daily with rifampicin; separate from cations (WHO PQ label HA737).
unverifiedSections: NACO 2021 Tables 2.10.6–2.10.11 (exposure and source codes, regimens, follow-up) could not be read; NACO-specific regimens and codes are not shown.
PEP for children under 30 kg is not covered; refer to an ART centre.
Hepatitis B vaccination and immunoglobulin doses after exposure are not included because the source tables could not be read.
First aid steps are standard practice, not quoted from an opened source.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: PEP is a 28-day course of antiretroviral therapy (ART) started soon after a possible exposure to HIV to stop infection becoming established. Health workers in India are at risk from needlestick and sharps injuries, and PEP is also needed after sexual exposure and sexual assault. It works best within hours and is not started after 72 hours. Care includes immediate first aid, assessing the exposure and the source, baseline testing, a three-drug regimen (dolutegravir with tenofovir and lamivudine as a single TLD tablet in India), adherence support, follow-up HIV testing, and hepatitis B and C assessment. People with ongoing risk can move straight on to pre-exposure prophylaxis.
keyMechanisms: HIV first infects local cells and reaches lymph nodes over 24–72 hours.
Early ART can block viral replication before infection is established.
Integrase inhibitors (dolutegravir) block viral DNA integration; tenofovir and lamivudine block reverse transcriptase.
Risk depends on fluid, route, depth of injury and source viral load.

symptoms: Recent needlestick, sharps or mucosal splash with blood or body fluid
Recent condomless sex or sexual assault
redFlags: Presentation after 72 hours: PEP not indicated; test and counsel (WHO 2024)
Symptoms of acute HIV (fever, rash, sore throat) during follow-up
Creatinine clearance below 50 mL/min: TLD unsuitable (label)
Sexual assault: also emergency contraception and STI care

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Exposure to intact skin needs no PEP.
Positive baseline test: treat as HIV, not PEP.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Start ideally within 24 hours and no later than 72 hours.
Adults and adolescents 30 kg or more; creatinine clearance 50 mL/min or more.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Reactive: manage as HIV infection, not PEP

clinicalManagement.title: First aid
actions: Wash wound with soap and water; do not squeeze or scrub; flush splashes to eyes or mouth with water.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess
actions: Type of exposure and fluid; source status if known.
Exposure within 72 hours and risk present: start PEP without waiting for results (WHO 2024).

clinicalManagement.title: Start PEP
actions: TLD one tablet daily for 28 days (label; WHO 2024).
Sexual exposure: emergency contraception and STI assessment.

clinicalManagement.title: Follow-up
actions: Ongoing risk: move straight to pre-exposure prophylaxis (CDC 2025).

branches.label: Three-drug PEP
branches.entryCriteria: Exposure within 72 hours with risk of HIV transmission, adult or adolescent 30 kg or more.

regimens.patientGroup: Adults and adolescents 30 kg or more
regimens.genericName: Dolutegravir, lamivudine and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TLD) 50/300/300 mg
adjustments: Paediatric: Not for children under 30 kg (label); refer to an ART centre for paediatric PEP.
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
CKD: Not recommended if creatinine clearance below 50 mL/min; use separate formulations (label).
CLD: No adjustment in Child-Pugh A or B; caution in Child-Pugh C (label).
Separate from antacids, calcium, iron and multivitamins: 2 hours after or 6 hours before (label section 4.5).
contraindications: With rifampicin give extra dolutegravir 50 mg (label)

medicationPlan.note: Regimen and duration from the WHO-prequalified TLD label (PEP posology) and WHO 2024; testing from CDC 2025. NACO 2021 tables could not be opened. India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

teaching.scope: HIV PEP in Indian hospitals and clinics.
learningObjectives: Give first aid and assess risk.
keyPoints: Start as early as possible; not after 72 hours.
TLD one tablet daily for 28 days.
Test HIV at baseline, 4–6 and 12 weeks.
pitfalls: Not offering emergency contraception after sexual exposure.
